daily_narrative.happened: Stocks rebounded, led by technology, with the S&P 500 up 0.9% and Nasdaq up 1.3% as Reuters said the session was driven by large-cap tech strength and a quiet, data-light tape.[4][1] The move appears to reflect renewed buying in chip and software names, alongside an earnings-season rotation rather than a single macro shock.[4][5] In a slowdown regime, the broad index gain but weak momentum and quality-outperforming growth suggests investors are favoring selective tech leadership while defensives and several software/healthcare names lag.[1][4]
